name: Windsurf (Codeium)
description: Cascade flows with per-session context. Workspace = open directory. Auto + manual Memories stored at ~/.codeium/windsurf/memories/. Scoped by global_rules.md vs .windsurfrules (project-local). Strong memory-layering model.

identity_and_auth.user_identity_model: Identity is required and account-based: users authenticate to a Codeium/Windsurf account (email+password, or OAuth via Google/GitHub) to access Cascade and AI features. The account ties license, global rules, and quotas to the user. The local IDE itself is a fork of VS Code, but AI functionality is gated behind sign-in. Enterprise deployments add org SSO via SAML 2.0 / OIDC and admin-managed seats. [uncertain]
identity_and_auth.multi_user_collaboration: Primarily a single-developer tool. Memories are stored per-machine, per-workspace and are not shared between developers by design. Team/enterprise tiers add org-level governance: admin consoles, seat management, SSO, and system-level rules that admins can push to all workspaces (cannot be overridden by end users without admin permission). The common pattern for team-shared context is to commit .windsurfrules / .windsurf/rules to the repo rather than rely on the (per-machine) Memories store. No real-time concurrent multi-user editing of a single Cascade session. [uncertain]

workspace_model.workspace_definition: A workspace is the open directory (folder) in the Windsurf editor, inheriting VS Code's folder-as-workspace model. The workspace is identified by a hash derived from the local directory path (not from git remote/repo identity). Consequently the same repo cloned to two different paths/machines produces two distinct workspace hashes and two separate Memory stores. Workspace does not map 1:1 to a git repo; it maps to a filesystem path. The active workspace defines the file corpus Cascade's context engine indexes and operates over.
workspace_model.workspace_session_binding: Cascade conversations (sessions/chats) are scoped to the workspace. Each new chat starts with a fresh context window; the context window is strictly per-session. A user can have multiple chats per workspace, and prior chats are browsable in the sidebar and can be re-opened, but Cascade does not automatically re-inject the substance of a past chat into a new one — only auto-generated Memories (workspace-scoped) and rules carry across sessions. Sessions are local to the IDE instance for that workspace.
workspace_model.context_scoping: Three layers. Session-level: active file, conversation history, explicitly @-referenced files, and the Cascade context engine's real-time tracking of edits/terminal/navigation. Workspace-level: .windsurfrules / .windsurf/rules committed in the repo, and auto/manual Memories scoped to that workspace hash. Global-level: global_rules.md tied to the user's Windsurf account (applies across all workspaces), plus optional enterprise system-level rules. Memories are workspace-scoped so preferences for one project do not bleed into another.
workspace_model.config_file_instruction_precedence: Cascade-of-rules model. Files (markdown): global_rules.md (account-global), .windsurfrules (legacy single project-root file), and the modern .windsurf/rules/ directory containing multiple rule files (the .windsurf/rules/ format takes precedence over legacy .windsurfrules; newer Devin-branded builds also recognize .devin/rules with precedence over .windsurf). Rules are discovered in the current workspace, sub-directories, and parent directories up to the git root. Rules support four activation modes: Always On, Manual, Model Decision, and Glob (path-pattern). When global and workspace rules conflict, project/workspace rules take precedence; on overflow Cascade prioritizes global rules then fits as many workspace rules as possible. Size caps: historically 6,000 chars per file; updated guidance is up to 12,000 chars per file and a 12,000-char combined total (global + workspace) — content beyond the cap is silently truncated. Enterprise system-level rules are merged in and cannot be overridden by users. [uncertain]
workspace_model.source_corpus_grounding_scope: Not a bounded-source research-assistant model. Grounding corpus = the indexed files in the open workspace directory (plus @-referenced files, open files, terminal output, and optional MCP-provided sources). There is no NotebookLM/Perplexity-Space-style curated source set; retrieval is scoped to the workspace filesystem and the local indexing/retrieval engine.

persistence_and_history.persistence_mechanism: Local-file based on the developer's machine. Memories are persisted as local files under ~/.codeium/windsurf/memories/, organized by a workspace hash derived from the directory path. Rules persist as plain markdown files (global_rules.md in the account/config dir; .windsurfrules / .windsurf/rules in the repo). Chat history is stored locally by the IDE (VS Code storage). No documented cloud Postgres/Mongo for personal session storage; storage appears to be flat/structured local files rather than SQLite for Memories. The model server (Cascade brain) runs in Codeium's cloud and is effectively stateless w.r.t. durable per-user session storage. [uncertain]
persistence_and_history.session_history: Past Cascade chats are retained locally and browsable in the IDE sidebar, where they can be manually re-opened. Within a session, history is the conversation transcript held in the per-session context window. There is no built-in cross-session re-injection of chat substance and no documented first-class export/portability of full chat transcripts; durable carry-over is intended to flow through Memories and committed rules rather than raw transcripts. Exact on-disk transcript format is not publicly documented. [uncertain]
persistence_and_history.memory_layering: Explicit two-layer (plus rules) model and a primary reference for memory-layering. (1) Auto-generated Memories: Cascade autonomously decides what is worth remembering and writes short workspace-scoped notes (e.g. 'user prefers Bun') to ~/.codeium/windsurf/memories/; reviewable/editable/deletable in the Memories panel. (2) Manual Memories: user can explicitly instruct Cascade to remember something. (3) Rules (user-authored, deterministic): global_rules.md and .windsurfrules / .windsurf/rules — static instructions always (or conditionally) applied. Architecturally: ephemeral thread state = the per-session context window (discarded between chats); durable cross-thread store = Memories + Rules, both fed into every Cascade prompt. Recommended discipline: promote stable Memories into committed rules; prune stale Memories since all active Memories are applied on every interaction.
persistence_and_history.search_retrieval_history: No documented global full-text or semantic search across past sessions. Past chats are manually re-openable from the sidebar (per-workspace). Cross-session continuity of facts is achieved via auto/manual Memories (auto-referenced by Cascade), not via searching transcripts. For richer recall users commonly bolt on an external memory layer through Windsurf's MCP support. [uncertain]
persistence_and_history.lifecycle_ttl_cleanup: Per-session context window is ephemeral and discarded when a chat ends / a new chat starts. Memories and Rules are persistent until explicitly edited/deleted by the user; there is no documented automatic TTL/expiration on Memories. Cleanup is manual (Memories panel: delete stale, promote stable to rules). A hard IDE crash can drop in-flight session state before it is persisted. No archive-vs-hard-delete distinction documented for Memories. [uncertain]

execution_and_isolation.sandbox_isolation_model: No per-session VM/container sandbox. Cascade operates as an in-IDE agent acting directly on the open workspace on the developer's local machine (and local terminal). The 'brain' (model inference) is a cloud service; execution of edits and shell commands happens in-process against the local filesystem with user-in-the-loop or auto-run command approval. There is no ephemeral repo checkout or git worktree isolation per session, and no separate per-session network policy beyond the local environment's own. Security posture is that of a local IDE plugin operating with the user's permissions. [uncertain]
execution_and_isolation.snapshot_state_restore: No machine/environment snapshot-and-restore primitive. There is no concept of saving filesystem/installed-packages/env-var state independently of the conversation. The only durable carried state is the conversation-adjacent Memories + Rules. Environment state is simply whatever exists on the developer's local machine.
execution_and_isolation.cloud_local_handoff: No cloud<->local session handoff. Inference runs in Codeium's cloud but the agent/session is local-only; there is no managed cloud execution environment to migrate a session to/from. Self-hosting of the full stack is limited to enterprise/VPC deployment of the service, not relocation of an individual session. [uncertain]
execution_and_isolation.parallelism_subagent_fanout: Cascade is primarily a single interactive agent per chat. Users can open multiple chats, but there is no first-class coordinator/managed-subagent fan-out comparable to Devin's managed Devins; Workflows allow scripting multi-step action sequences within a session. No documented N-parallel-worktree orchestration with shared/isolated workspace state. [uncertain]
execution_and_isolation.trigger_surface: Initiated from inside the Windsurf editor (IDE) only — Cascade chat/command surfaces within the desktop app. Rules/Memories also apply only to Cascade in the Windsurf editor. No documented Slack/GitHub-mention/CLI/cron trigger surface for starting Cascade sessions. [uncertain]

implementation.implementation_stack: Client: a VS Code fork (Electron) providing the editor and local storage for chats. Auth/identity: Codeium account service; enterprise SSO via SAML 2.0 / OIDC. Local persistence: flat/structured files for Memories at ~/.codeium/windsurf/memories/ keyed by a path-derived workspace hash; markdown files for rules (global_rules.md, .windsurfrules, .windsurf/rules/*.md). Context assembly: the Cascade context engine indexes/retrieves over workspace files and tracks live edits/terminal/navigation; rules + Memories are concatenated into the model prompt subject to character caps. Inference: Codeium's cloud-hosted frontier models (context windows up to ~1M tokens). Extensibility: native MCP client for external tools/memory. No documented server-side per-user session DB (Postgres/Mongo/Redis) for personal use. [uncertain]
implementation.applicability_to_labmate: Windsurf's memory-layering is the cleanest reference for Labmate's split between durable and ephemeral state. Map (a) Windsurf's per-session context window -> Labmate's Redis Streams active-session state with TTL (ephemeral, discarded at session end), and (b) Windsurf's Memories + Rules -> Labmate's MongoDB long-term docs (durable cross-thread store, always injected). Adopt the two-tier memory distinction explicitly: auto-generated memories (agent-decided, stored in Mongo, surfaced into every LangGraph turn) vs user-authored rules (deterministic, versioned). Key cautionary lesson: Windsurf keys its memory store by local directory path (workspace hash), which fragments memory across machines/clones — Labmate should instead use a stable logical workspace_id (e.g. repo identity or an explicit project id) rather than a filesystem path, so memory follows the project regardless of where/how it is accessed (e.g. via the Discord connector). For identity, follow Windsurf in scoping memories per (user, workspace) and keeping global/user-level preferences separate from workspace-level context. Borrow the 'promote stable memory to a versioned rule' lifecycle and a size/relevance budget so stale memories don't silently degrade prompts. Note the gap to fill: Windsurf has no cross-session transcript search — Labmate's history-retrieval API (full-text/semantic over Mongo session docs keyed by thread_id/workspace_id) is a clear differentiator.
